patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: (Mom) We were crossing the street and I swung her up by the hand — now she won't use her left arm at all and cries if I touch it. She just holds it kind of limp.
presentation.triageNote: 2-year-old female, arm pulled while crossing the street, now holds the left arm slightly flexed and pronated and refuses to use it, with no swelling, deformity, or point tenderness.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 5 / Non-Urgent is appropriate because this stable presentation is expected to need examination and a simple bedside maneuver without a countable emergency resource.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This is a stable toddler with left-arm nonuse after axial traction and no swelling, deformity, point tenderness, or neurovascular deficit.
clinical.acuityReason: The mechanism and resting position support a focused extremity assessment, while the absence of traumatic warning signs makes major injury less likely.
expectedResources: Focused examination and bedside reduction maneuver
keyFindings: Arm pulled while crossing the street
Left arm held slightly flexed and pronated
teachingPoints: A classic traction mechanism with the arm held pronated can support treatment without routine imaging when fracture findings are absent.
Swelling, deformity, focal bony tenderness, or an atypical mechanism should prompt reconsideration and possible imaging.

possibleDiagnoses: Occult upper-extremity fracture if atypical findings appear
possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: A successful reduction would usually be followed by observed return of arm use and discharge; persistent nonuse would require reassessment and possible imaging.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: on the clinic chair, holding her left arm limp against her body
signs: left arm held limp and close to the body
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a white 2-year-old toddler girl with curly hair, seated on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: holding her left arm limp against her body, refusing to move it. Expression: unhappy and teary. Clearly visible: the left arm held limp and close to the body. No text, no logos.
